narr: A multi-day severe weather event produced all modes of severe weather across Central Alabama. An upper low parked over the Midwest States and an upper ridge over the Florida Peninsula produced a deep layer of moisture and shear over Alabama. A slow moving surface cold front provided the focus for severe storms late Saturday night and continuing through Monday morning.
ev: Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-5 inches across northern Chilton County produced flash flooding across the northern two-thirds of Chilton County. Several county roads were flooded and impassable between Clanton and Jemison.
Widespread 3-5 inches of rainfall across southern Randolph County. Several streets in Wadley and Roanoke were flooded and impassable.
Widespread rainfall amounts of 4-6 inches across northern Tallapoosa County. Town Creek Road flooded and impassable.
Multiple roads across Coosa County flooded and impassable, including 29, 56 ,112, 118, 15, 122, 119.
Multiple roads flooded and impassable across the northern two-thirds of Chambers County, including the cities of Lanett and Lafayette.
Multiple roads flooded across southern Clay County. Fuller Road at Loombeam Creek washed out.
